**Caves as the game carves them, painted, with lakes, cave biomes and their decoration**

Caves are now a layer you paint: the Caves tool (in the new Underground group) paints where a cave layer carves its caves, and Edit ▸ Whole map ▸ Caves paints one over the whole map or the selection, after a picture of its caves (a plan at a height you pick and a cut through the land). A layer carves caves as Minecraft does since 1.18 — large chambers with pillars, long winding tunnels, thin noodles and ravines, each with its density, size and heights — under a roof of rock except where they open to the sky on dry land, and fills them with aquifers: water, and lava deep down, at levels of their own, walled off from each other by rock so that nothing runs once the game updates a block. Its settings change the caves wherever it is painted, at any time, and the caves take no room in the file. The Cave biome tool paints lush caves, dripstone caves and the deep dark between two heights; the export writes the game's cave biomes and decorates their caves as the game does: moss, azaleas, glow berries and dripleaves by clay pools; dripstone blocks with stalactites and stalagmites thick at their base; sculk, veins, sensors, shriekers and catalysts with their block entities; glow lichen in other caves. Underground on the 2D map cuts it through at a height, and X-ray in the 3D views shows the caves through the ground. The Ores window adds the game's large veins of copper in granite and iron in tuff. WorldPainter's Caverns, Chasms and Caves layers open as cave layers painted where they were.
